preamble: 1. ข้อสอบมีทั้งหมด 90 ข้อ
2. ข้อสอบเป็นอังกฤษทั้งหมด
3. มีเวลาในการสอบ 2.5 ชั่วโมง

questions.stem: A 55-year-old right-handed man develops sudden difficulty producing speech. He understands spoken language and can follow complex verbal commands, but his speech is slow, effortful, and nonfluent. Which Brodmann areas are most likely affected?
A 62-year-old patient can hear normally but has difficulty understanding speech. His speech is fluent but contains incorrect or meaningless words. Which Brodmann area is affected?

A patient suffers an injury to the superior temporal region of the cerebral cortex. He has difficulty processing and localizing auditory information. Which Brodmann areas are primarily associated with the primary auditory cortex?

A 55-year-old patient presents with progressive muscle weakness and muscle atrophy. Neurological examination reveals findings consistent with both upper motor neuron (UMN) and lower motor neuron (LMN) involvement. Which of the following diagnoses is most consistent with this presentation?
A 30-year-old man presents with difficulty breathing. Which of the following nuclei in the spinal cord is most likely involved and could cause this condition?

A 23-year-old man is involved in a motorcycle accident and briefly loses consciousness. He initially becomes alert and appears relatively normal but several hours later develops a severe headache, vomiting, and rapidly worsening consciousness. CT scan reveals a biconvex (lens- shaped), hyperdense extra-axial hematoma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 85-year-old woman develops sudden-onset weakness of the left arm and leg with hyperreflexia. When asked to protrude her tongue, the tongue deviates to the left side. Which of the following additional findings is most likely to be present?

choices.C: Loss of proprioception in the left arm and leg
choices.D: Loss of proprioception in the right arm and leg
choices.E: Loss of pain and temperature sensation from the face

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man develops a painful infection after squeezing a pimple on the bridge of his nose. Several days later, he develops severe headache, fever, and diplopia. The infection is suspected to have spread to the cavernous sinus through the venous system. Which of the following routes most likely allows the infection to reach the cavernous sinus?

choices.A: Facial vein → superior petrosal vein → cavernous sinus
choices.B: Facial vein → ophthalmic vein → cavernous sinus
choices.C: Facial vein → transverse sinus → cavernous sinus
choices.D: Facial vein → sigmoid sinus → cavernous sinus
choices.E: Facial vein → inferior petrosal vein → superior sagittal sinus

questions.stem: A patient presents with hoarseness, dysphagia, and diminished gag reflex. He also has loss of pain and temperature sensation over the left side of the face and the right side of the body. Which of the following structures is most likely involved?

choices.B: Left spinal trigeminal nucleus and tract

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man develops a small infarction involving the left medial medulla. Neurological examination reveals loss of vibration and proprioception in the left leg. Which of the following additional findings is most likely to be present?

choices.D: Loss of pain and temperature sensation over the left side of the face
choices.E: Right-sided loss of pain and temperature sensation from the body

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man suddenly develops weakness of the right arm and leg. Neurological examination shows increased muscle tone, hyperreflexia, and a positive Babinski sign on the right. Sensory examination is normal. MRI reveals a small lesion involving the left side of the brainstem above the pyramidal decussation. Which of the following structures is most likely damaged?

A 45-year-old woman has a lesion involving the right half of the spinal cord at T8. Examination shows weakness of the right leg with hyperreflexia and a positive Babinski sign. She also has impaired vibration and proprioception on the right side below T8. Which additional finding is most likely?

choices.A: Right-sided loss of pain and temperature below T8
choices.B: Left-sided loss of pain and temperature beginning several segments below T8
choices.C: Left-sided loss of vibration and proprioception below T8
choices.E: Bilateral loss of pain and temperature below T8

questions.stem: A 70-year-old patient develops an infarction of the right medial medulla. Examination reveals: Left-sided weakness of the arm and leg, Loss of vibration and proprioception on the left side, Tongue deviation to the right when protruded Which artery is most likely responsible?

A 55-year-old woman experiences sudden, severe, electric shock-like pain around the mouth and cheek. The pain occurs in brief episodes and is triggered by touching her face while washing it. Which cranial nerve is most likely involved?

A 55-year-old woman experiences recurrent episodes of severe, brief, electric shock-like pain over the lower lip and chin. The pain is frequently triggered by eating, brushing her teeth, or touching the area around her mouth. Which division of the trigeminal nerve is most likely involved?

A 42-year-old woman presents with sudden-onset weakness of the right side of her face. On examination, she is unable to raise her right eyebrow, close her right eye tightly, or elevate the right corner of her mouth. The rest of the neurological examination is normal. Which of the following structures is most likely affected?

A 40 YO woman could not close her right eye and lift her right lip angle while smiling. She had difficulty speaking, eating, drinking and increased sensitivity to sound. Which following structure is the most likely affected by lesions?

A 65-year-old woman suddenly develops weakness of the left leg. Neurological examination reveals spasticity, hyperreflexia, and a positive Babinski sign in the left leg. The left arm and face are relatively spared. Which of the following cerebral arteries is most likely involved?

A 68-year-old man suddenly develops weakness of the right face and arm, with mild weakness of the right leg. Neurological examination also reveals difficulty producing speech, while comprehension is relatively preserved. Which of the following arteries is most likely involved?

A 64-year-old man suddenly develops weakness of the right arm and lower face. He also has difficulty speaking and is unable to name familiar objects, although his hearing is normal. His right leg is only mildly affected. Which of the following arteries is most likely involved?

A 38-year-old man presents with weakness of the left arm and leg. Neurological examination reveals inability to abduct the right eye and complete paralysis of the right side of the face, including the forehead. Where is the most likely location of the lesion?
A 70-year-old man develops pure sensory loss involving the right side of the face, arm, and leg, without weakness. MRI reveals a small lacunar infarction. Which structure is most likely affected?

choices.A: Left genu of the internal capsule
choices.B: Left posterior limb of the internal capsule

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with weakness of the right upper limb. She has difficulty flexing the right elbow, and the brachioradialis reflex is diminished on the right side. Sensory examination reveals decreased sensation over the thumb and lateral aspect of the forearm. Which spinal nerve root is most likely affected?

A 64-year-old woman suddenly develops right-sided weakness of the face, arm, and leg accompanied by mild loss of sensation in the same regions. She has no aphasia, visual field defect, neglect, or impaired consciousness. MRI shows a small lacunar infarction involving a compact white-matter structure deep within the left cerebral hemisphere. Which of the following locations is most likely affected?

choices.A: Left VPL nucleus of the thalamus
choices.B: Left VPM nucleus of the thalamus
choices.C: Left posterior limb of the internal capsule
choices.D: Right posterior limb of the internal capsule

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man develops sudden-onset left-sided hemiparesis. Examination also reveals right-sided ptosis, a dilated right pupil, and the right eye deviated down and laterally. Which structure is most likely affected?

choices.C: Left corticospinal tract in the cerebral peduncle
choices.D: Right corticospinal tract in the cerebral peduncle

questions.stem: The microscopic examination of 40-year-old man revealed eosinophilia of cytoplasm and pykotic nuclei, along with decreased of neurons. pyramidal neuron in hippocampus and cortex, as well as cerebellar Purkinje were primarily affected. What's the major cause of neuronal loss?

A 60-year-old man suddenly die. Autopsy reveals hemorrhage in the basal ganglia. Histological examination shows hyalinized arteriolosclerosis of intraparenchymal arterioles. What is the most likely underlying disease?
A patient presents with a sudden, severe headache. MRI reveals a subarachnoid hemorrhage associated with a thin-walled outpouching of an intracranial artery. What is the most likely vascular lesion?

A 70-year-old man has had lung adenocarcinoma with brain metastasis 6 month over the day. He has had severe headache with vomiting followed confusion. Which of the following signs to diagnosis in his case?

40-year-old woman with fluctuating weakness for 3 weak, mild partial ptosis right side, Full EOM, muscle weakness grade 4 at Neck flexor and proximal arm, fatigability test positive. Where is the possible lesion?

A 32-year-old woman developed painful proximal leg weakness for 2 months. A motor function changed from walking independently to walking with cane and inability to walk upstairs. The physical examination revealed proximal arm and leg weakness grade 3+. Pinkprick and vibratory sensation were normal and DTR 2+ all. Heliotrope rash and grotton papule were observerd. Where is the possible lesion?

A 30-year-old women has progressive numbness. She has postural instability sensation during closing her left eye esp. wash her hair. PE: generalized muscle weakness grade 4, decreased pin prick sensation of both hand and feet. DTR is 0 Where is the possible lesion?

A 20-year-old man presents with a sudden, severe headache described as the “worst headache of his life”. CT scan reveals a subarachnoid hemorrhage. Cerebral angiography demonstrates a thin-walled, saccular outpouching arising from the anterior part of the Circle of Willis. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

choices.D: Tearing of a subdural bridging vein

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man dies 10 days after suffering a severe ischemic stroke. At autopsy, histological examination of the affected brain tissue is performed. Which of the following histological findings is most likely to be observed?

choices.A: Microglial nodules surrounding and phagocytosing dying neurons
choices.B: Intranuclear glycogen inclusions with enlargement of the vestibular nuclei
choices.C: Central chromatolysis with peripheral displacement of the nucleus
choices.D: Aggregates of supernumerary Schwann cells forming onion bulbs
choices.E: Shrinkage of neuronal cell bodies with nuclear pyknosis and intensely eosinophilic cytoplasm

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man is involved in a motorcycle accident and develops an acute epidural hematoma. He rapidly develops severe headaches, confusion, and vomiting. Which of the following findings is most likely to be associated with this condition?

choices.E: Decreased venous pulsation of the retinal veins

questions.stem: Which of the following is mediated by a monosynaptic reflex?
A long-distance runner maintains a steady pace for several hours. Which type of motor unit is primarily responsible for maintaining muscle contraction without becoming easily fatigued?

A patient is being examined for the stretch reflex. A sensory receptor detects the change in length of the skeletal muscle and sends information to the spinal cord. Which of the following structures is responsible for detecting this change?

A person is lifting a heavy object. As the tension in the biceps muscle increases, the person suddenly relaxes the muscle and drops the object. Which sensory receptor is primarily responsible for detecting increased muscle tension?

A 58-year-old man suddenly develops loss of pain and temperature sensation over the right side of the face, associated with right-sided LMN facial paralysis and right limb ataxia. He has no dysphagia or hoarseness. Where is the most likely location of the lesion?
A patient has a lesion of the right side of the spinal cord at the L1 level. Which of the following sensory deficits is most likely to occur?

choices.A: Contralateral loss of pain and temperature beginning approximately at L3–L4 level
choices.B: Ipsilateral loss of pain and temperature beginning approximately at L3–L4 level
choices.C: Contralateral loss of proprioception and vibration at the L1 level
choices.D: Bilateral loss of proprioception and vibration below the L1 level
choices.E: Contralateral loss of proprioception with ipsilateral loss of pain and temperature

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with a long history of poorly controlled diabetes mellitus presents with burning pain and numbness in both feet. The symptoms are worse at night and have gradually progressed from the toes upward. Which of the following best explains the underlying pathological mechanism?

choices.D: Neuromuscular junction dysfunction due to myasthenia gravis
choices.E: Inflammatory demyelination of the central nervous system

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man develops progressive weakness and numbness of both legs several days after a respiratory infection. Neurological examination reveals symmetrical weakness, decreased muscle tone, and absent deep tendon reflexes in both lower limbs. Which of the following is the most likely pathological mechanism?

choices.B: Ischemic infarction of the spinal cord

questions.stem: A local anesthetic is administered to a patient. The drug is more effective in an alkaline environment than in an acidic environment. Which of the following best explains why alkalinity enhances the effectiveness of local anesthetics?

choices.A: Alkalinity increases blood flow, resulting in greater drug distribution
choices.B: Alkalinity increases the proportion of the non-ionized form, allowing the drug to cross the neuronal membrane more easily
choices.C: Alkalinity increases the proportion of the ionized form, which binds more strongly to sodium channels
choices.D: Alkalinity prevents the local anesthetic from being metabolized by plasma esterases
choices.E: Alkalinity increases renal excretion of the local anesthetic

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with a history of hypertension suddenly develops violent, involuntary, flinging movements of the right arm and leg. MRI reveals a small lacunar infarction involving the deep gray matter of the basal ganglia. Which of the following structures is most likely affected?

A 65-year-old man presents with a 2-year history of progressively slowed movements. On examination, he has a resting tremor of the right hand, increased muscle tone, and difficulty initiating movement. When asked to walk, he takes short, shuffling steps and has difficulty stopping once he starts walking. Which of the following is the most characteristic clinical sign of Parkinson disease?

A 66-year-old man presents with a 2-year history of gradually progressive movement difficulty. He has a resting tremor, bradykinesia, and rigidity. His symptoms are predominantly unilateral at first and gradually progress over time. He has no history of exposure to dopamine- blocking medications, stroke, or other neurological diseases. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man presents with progressive right lower-limb ataxia. Neurological examination reveals impaired coordination of the right leg and difficulty maintaining accurate limb position, while pain, temperature, vibration, and conscious proprioception are relatively preserved. The findings suggest impaired transmission of unconscious proprioceptive information from the lower limb to the cerebellum. Which of the following ascending pathways is most likely damaged?

A 58-year-old woman presents with resting tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia that have progressively worsened over several years. Neurological examination shows no major sensory deficit. Which structure is most likely dysfunctional?

A 25-year-old man is involved in a motorcycle accident and sustains a head injury. He initially loses consciousness briefly but then becomes fully conscious and appears neurologically normal. Several hours later, he suddenly develops a severe headache, vomiting, and rapidly progresses to coma. Which of the following intracranial hemorrhages is most likely responsible?

A 68-year-old man with a history of hypertension suddenly develops violent, involuntary, flinging movements of the left arm and leg. MRI reveals a small lacunar infarction involving the basal ganglia. Which of the following structures is most likely affected?
This abnormal movement is caused by excessive exhibition of motor activity due to disruption of the basal ganglia circuitry. Which of the following structures is most likely involved?
Which of the following fibers is primarily involved in motor learning in the cerebellum?
Which functional division of the cerebellum is primarily associated with the dentate nucleus?

A 47-year-old man presents with a loss of somatic sensation from the left fingertips, while sensation over the face remains intact. MRI reveals a small hemorrhagic lesion involving the thalamus. Which of the following structures is most likely affected?

choices.D: Ventral posterolateral (VPL) nucleus of the thalamus
choices.E: Ventral posteromedial (VPM) nucleus of the thalamus

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man is diagnosed with early Parkinson disease. An anticholinergic drug is considered as monotherapy because his symptoms are relatively mild. Which of the following symptoms is most effectively treated by anticholinergic therapy?

67-year-old man develops a gradually progressive resting tremor, bradykinesia, rigidity, and postural instability over several years. He has no history of exposure to antipsychotic drugs, toxins, or significant head trauma. Neurological examination shows asymmetric motor symptoms, with the right side more severely affected. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient with Parkinson disease is treated with levodopa in combination with carbidopa and entacapone to improve the therapeutic effect of levodopa. Which of the following correctly describes the mechanism of these two drugs?

choices.A: Carbidopa inhibits COMT, while entacapone inhibits MAO-B
choices.B: Carbidopa inhibits DOPA decarboxylase, while entacapone inhibits COMT
choices.C: Carbidopa inhibits MAO-B, while entacapone inhibits DOPA decarboxylase
choices.D: Carbidopa inhibits dopamine β-hydroxylase, while entacapone inhibits MAO-B
choices.E: Carbidopa inhibits COMT, while entacapone inhibits DOPA decarboxylase

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely cause of his secondary parkinsonism?

A 62-year-old man is diagnosed with Parkinson disease. His most prominent and troublesome symptom is a resting tremor, while rigidity and bradykinesia are relatively mild. Which of the following drug classes is most appropriate for controlling his predominant symptom?

A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a motorcycle accident. A CT scan of the head reveals a biconvex (lens-shaped) hyperdense hematoma between the skull and the dura mater, consistent with an epidural hematoma. Which of the following blood vessels is most likely injured?

A 52-year-old man with a long history of chronic alcohol use is brought to the hospital because of acute confusion. On neurological examination, he has ataxia with an unsteady gait and bilateral ophthalmoplegia. His symptoms have developed over the past few days, and his nutritional intake has been poor. Which of the following vitamin deficiencies is most likely responsible for this condition?
An immunocompromised patient develops chronic meningitis with increased CSF protein. India ink staining of the CSF shows encapsulated yeast cells. Which organism is the most likely causative agent?

A 30-year-old man presents with fever, headache, confusion, and weight loss for 3 weeks. CSF examination shows lymphocytic pleocytosis, high protein, and low glucose. Which of the following is the most appropriate test to confirm the diagnosis?
A patient with AIDS presents with multiple ring-enhancing abscesses located near the gray- white junction of the cerebral cortex. Which organism is the most likely causative agent?

A 22-year-old man presents with a 2-day history of fever, headache, photophobia, and neck stiffness. Lumbar puncture reveals a CSF protein level of 60 mg/dL, glucose of 68 mg/dL with a concurrent blood glucose of 100 mg/dL, and a WBC count of 180 cells/mm³ with 95% mononuclear cells. Gram stain is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old man presents with a 3-day history of fever, headache, photophobia, and neck stiffness. He is alert and oriented, with no focal neurological deficits or seizures. Lumbar puncture reveals a CSF WBC count of 220 cells/mm³, with 90% lymphocytes, a mildly elevated protein level of 70 mg/dL, and a CSF glucose level of 65 mg/dL with a simultaneous blood glucose level of 100 mg/dL. Gram staining shows no organisms. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old man is involved in a high-speed motor vehicle accident. He experiences rapid rotational movement of the head with marked angular acceleration and loses consciousness immediately. Despite no major mass lesion on initial CT, he remains in a prolonged coma. Microscopic examination shows axonal swelling with increased microglial activity and subsequent axonal degeneration. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which type of gliomas has the worst prognosis?
Histopathology shows small, round to oval cells in an abundant, densely fibrillar background, with ependymal rosettes and perivascular pseudorosettes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

Histopathology shows a biphasic appearance with compact fibrillar portions containing elongated bipolar cells and Rosenthal fibers, and loose microcystic portions with cobweb-like processes and eosinophilic granular bodies. Which immunohistochemical staining indicates the cell origin of this tumor?

A newborn presents with severe developmental delay and seizures. Brain imaging shows abnormal development of the cerebral cortex with abnormal distribution of neurons in the telencephalon. Which of the following developmental processes is most likely impaired in this patient?
A severe embryonal malformation results in absence of part of the skull and brain. The newborn usually dies soon after birth. Which statement could cause this event?

choices.C: Lack of migration of neuronal progenitor cells
choices.D: Failure of closure of the anterior neuropore

questions.stem: A newborn fails to pass meconium within 48 hours after birth and develops abdominal distension. A rectal biopsy shows absence of enteric ganglion cells in the distal colon. Which of the following embryological structures is most likely affected?
A newborn is noted to have a severe congenital defect characterized by absence of most of the cerebral hemispheres and cranial vault. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A newborn is delivered at term and is noted to have severe craniofacial abnormalities. Physical examination reveals a single eye located in the midline of the face (cyclopia), a single nasal structure, and severe abnormalities of the development of the forebrain. Imaging demonstrates failure of the cerebral hemispheres to separate into two distinct hemispheres. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man presents with a gradually progressive history of neck and upper back pain for 2 years. He reports difficulty performing fine movements with both hands and has noticed weakness and muscle wasting of the hands and forearms. Neurological examination reveals bilateral loss of pain and temperature sensation over the shoulders, upper chest, and arms in a “cape-like” distribution. However, vibration and proprioception are preserved. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
